title: Immerse Education Summer School
description: Two-week academic summer school for students aged 13-18, held at Cambridge, Oxford and London, plus international locations (Sydney, Toronto, San Francisco, New York, Tokyo, Singapore, Boston). Ages 13-15 and 16-18 get tailored course lists spanning STEM (biology, chemistry, physics, maths, engineering, computer science, AI), humanities/social sciences (English literature, history, philosophy, law, economics, international relations, psychology, criminology) and professional tracks (medicine, business management, architecture, global leadership). Residential fee for the Cambridge programme is GBP 7,495 for two weeks (GBP 5,995 non-residential), covering ~40 hours of teaching (largely by Cambridge/Oxford academics), 2 hours 1:1 tutoring, a personal project with tutor feedback, mentor pairing, two coach excursions, and a graduation ceremony; BAC-accredited, offering up to 16 UCAS points and 3 US college credits.
citizenship_restrictions: None stated; official pages describe applicants coming "from around the world."
residency_restrictions: None stated on the fetched pages.
application_requirements: select a programme via online enrolment form
pay programme deposit (GBP 995) to secure a place
selectivity_evidence: Official Cambridge summer-school page describes the process as: select a programme, complete an online enrolment form, and pay the deposit to secure your place -- no academic review, personal statement, or rejection process is described, i.e. this is capacity-limited rolling enrollment, not merit selection. A separate, genuinely competitive Essay Competition Scholarship (up to 100% off) and other bursaries exist but are optional add-ons distinct from general admission: "Immerse Education occasionally offers competitions and scholarships that can reduce the fee. These are competitive and usually require an application process."
verification_status: Verified - official page fetched and read

title: Oxford Scholastica Academy Summer School
description: Residential summer school in Oxford for high-school students, offering two-week (or combined four-week) courses in Business & Enterprise, Computer Science & Coding, Creative Writing, Debate & Public Speaking, Engineering, International Relations/Politics & Leadership, Law, Medicine, and Psychology & Neuroscience. 2026 sessions ran 5-18 July, 19 July-1 August, and 2-15 August. Residential fee is GBP 7,495 for two weeks (GBP 6,995 non-residential; four-week combined GBP 14,690 residential / GBP 13,690 non-residential), covering tuition/materials, accommodation, breakfast and dinner, cultural trips (Blenheim Palace, Windsor), welcome/graduation events, and a personalised Letter of Recommendation; lunch and international travel cost extra. The academy's separate general FAQ page describes a broader 11-18 age band across its full portfolio of in-person and online courses, while the dedicated high-school residential program targets ages 15-18.
citizenship_restrictions: None stated; official FAQ says students come from "over 85 different countries."
residency_restrictions: None stated on the fetched pages.
application_requirements: be aged 11-18 at the start of the chosen course (15-18 for the residential high-school program)
personal statement demonstrating motivation
English proficiency equivalent to IELTS 6.5
GBP 995 deposit to secure a place
selectivity_evidence: Official FAQ states this is an applicant-reviewed program, not simple pay-to-enrol: "Our admissions panel will assess your application and will be in touch to confirm whether you have been accepted onto the programme," based on age eligibility, a personal statement, and English-language proficiency (IELTS 6.5 equivalent). The official Dates & Fees page adds: "There is no fixed deadline as we assess applications on a rolling basis until we're full." No numeric acceptance rate is published. The academy states it does not offer traditional scholarships, instead providing "thousands of hours of free mentoring and academic guidance each year."
verification_status: Verified - official page fetched and read

title: LSE Summer School
organization: London School of Economics and Political Science (LSE)
description: LSE's own social-science summer school in London: one-, two- or three-week sessions (2026: 22 June-10 July, 13-31 July, 3-21 August) with courses at 100/200/300 level in Accounting, Business and Management, Economics, Finance, International Relations, Law, and Data Science/AI/Research Methods, plus a Prep English course, taught -- per LSE -- to the same academic standard as its own degree modules, with possible credit transfer. This is a paid, non-selective offering distinct from LSE's own undergraduate admissions: pricing is tiered into a "student rate" (GBP 3,350/one session, currently-enrolled university/college students only) and a "standard rate" (GBP 4,450/one session) available to others, including secondary-school students who hold a university offer letter. A non-refundable GBP 60 application fee applies.
citizenship_restrictions: None stated on the fetched pages.
residency_restrictions: None stated on the fetched pages.
application_requirements: online application plus non-refundable GBP 60 application fee
university offer letter (if not yet at university) or transcript, for 100-level courses
prerequisite university-level coursework in the same/related subject for 200-level courses; intermediate coursework for 300-level
evidence of English-language proficiency where required
selectivity_evidence: Official entry-requirements FAQ states admission is explicitly "not selective/competitive": the program runs "on a first-come, first-served basis" with "no fixed deadlines," and applicants can enrol "up until the point it is filled." Entry is gated by prerequisites rather than comparative merit review -- e.g. 100-level courses require "an offer of a place at university," and a university offer letter can substitute for a transcript for applicants who "have not yet started studying at university," meaning a strong final-year secondary student with a university offer is eligible even though this is not a program aimed primarily at high schoolers.
verification_status: Verified - official page fetched and read

title: Sutton Trust UK Summer Schools
description: One-week, fully-funded residential summer schools giving UK state-school students a taste of undergraduate life at 13 partner UK universities (e.g. Cambridge, Edinburgh, Durham, St Andrews, Sheffield, Glasgow). Official page: "Our Summer Schools are completely free so you can get to know your chosen university, no matter where in the country you're from," covering course fees/materials, accommodation, three meals a day, on-programme trips, and reimbursed travel. Over 40 subject taster areas are offered, from "Archaeology and Anthropology to Veterinary Medicine," with over 15 hours of undergraduate-level teaching plus UCAS/personal-statement/student-finance guidance. Eligibility is restricted to Year 12 (England/Wales) / Year 13 (Northern Ireland) / S5 (Scotland) students who have always attended a state-funded, non-fee-paying school, with priority for widening-participation criteria (first-generation university applicant, Free School Meals history, low-progression school/area, care experience) alongside a desirable GCSE benchmark of five grades 9-6 (incl. English and Maths, at least two at 9-7).
citizenship_restrictions: Not explicitly stated by citizenship on the fetched pages, but the school/residency criteria below make it de facto restricted to students schooled in the UK.
residency_restrictions: Applicants must "attend, and have always attended, a state-funded, non-fee paying school/college" and be in Year 12 (England/Wales), Year 13 (Northern Ireland), or S5 (Scotland or equivalent).
application_requirements: Year 12/13/S5 enrolment at a state-funded, non-fee-paying school
GCSE record (desirable: five grades 9-6 including English and Maths, at least two at 9-7)
at least one widening-participation criterion (first-generation university applicant, Free School Meals history, low-progression school/area, or care experience)
selectivity_evidence: Official eligibility page frames this as competitive, criteria-based selection against a limited number of free places, not open enrollment: "The more criteria you meet, the more likely you are to secure a place," evaluated against a list of widening-participation factors (first-generation, Free School Meals history, low-progression school/neighbourhood, care experience) plus a GCSE benchmark. No numeric acceptance rate is published. Cambridge-specific applications closed earlier (12 February 2026) than the general 5 March 2026 deadline, consistent with high demand for the more selective partner university.
verification_status: Verified - official page fetched and read

title: Sciences Po Summer School - Pre-College Programme
description: Sciences Po's Paris-based Summer School offers separate tracks for university students and for secondary-school students ("Pre-College Programmes"). The Pre-College on-campus programme (2026: 4-21 July) costs EUR 6,000, covering courses, books/materials, accommodation, meals, excursions/activities and in-programme transport (a EUR 2,000 online-only Pre-College option also exists, 29 June-9 July 2026); a non-refundable EUR 50 application fee applies to all applicants. Eligibility: currently enrolled in secondary school and still enrolled in Fall 2026, aged at least 15 and under 18 at the time of the programme; students graduating high school by Summer 2026 must instead apply to the University Programmes. Advanced English (B2-C1) is required since the academic programme runs in English; an optional French elective requires B2 French. Sciences Po does not offer scholarships for this program and directs applicants to their own schools/embassies for funding.
citizenship_restrictions: None stated on the fetched pages.
residency_restrictions: None stated on the fetched pages.
application_requirements: certificate of enrolment from current secondary school confirming enrolment/graduation date
academic transcripts for 2024-25 and 2025-26
proof of English proficiency (B2-C1: official test, 2+ years fully English-taught study, or Sciences Po language assessment)
500-word motivation letter in English
letter of recommendation from an academic instructor
non-refundable EUR 50 application fee
selectivity_evidence: Official 'How to Apply' page describes rolling, jury-reviewed admissions rather than pay-to-enrol: an 'admissions jury' meets regularly and evaluates 'the candidate's academic background and motivation for the programme,' with applicants typically hearing back 'approximately one month after submitting a complete application.' Spots decrease as the deadline approaches and admissions close once full; the 2026 on-campus cycle is already listed as closed as of this research date, while the separate online Pre-College track's later deadline (27 May 2026) had also already passed by the 20 August 2026 research date.

title: Bocconi Summer School for High School Students
description: Two-week summer program in Milan for high-school students (2026 dates: 6-17 July), in their "third-to-last and second-to-last year" of high school and at least 15 years old by the start of the program (in Italy or abroad). Students pick two of 17 one-week labs (e.g. Data Science, Machine Learning and AI, Finance, Entrepreneurship, Game Theory, International Politics, Luxury and Fashion, Digital Marketing, Strategy, Law of Business and New Technologies). Participation fee is EUR 2,700 (academics, materials, extracurriculars, certificate, transport card), with optional Bocconi residence housing at EUR 1,600 for two weeks (single bedroom, shared bath); meals, airport pickup and visa support are not included. Required documents: ID/passport scans (student + guardian), a headshot, and 2024-25 school transcripts. The 2026 main intake is already listed as "sold out"; only a separate, smaller Italian-language Law track (6-10 July) remained open, with an application deadline of 9 April 2026.
citizenship_restrictions: None stated; official page says applicants can be "in Italy or abroad."
residency_restrictions: None stated on the fetched pages.
application_requirements: register on the MyApplication portal
valid ID/passport scans (student and parent/guardian)
headshot photo
school transcripts for 2024-25 in English or Italian
select two preferred lab courses
pay the participation fee
selectivity_evidence: Official pages describe rolling, capacity-limited enrollment rather than a competitive merit review: spots "may fill up quickly" and the main 2026 intake is already marked "sold out," with only the smaller Italian-language Law track still open. title: IE University Pre-University Summer Program
description: Two-week pre-university experience for students aged 15-17, week one in Segovia and week two at IE Tower in Madrid, taught by IE University faculty. Curriculum blends skill-building workshops (design thinking, sustainability/social-impact challenges, critical thinking in AI, a customer-discovery hackathon, presentation/pitch training) with campus-life immersion and university-admissions guidance; students receive an official certificate of completion. As of this research date (20 August 2026) the official page has already moved on to the next cycle: six two-week intake editions are listed for Summer 2027 (from 13 June-25 June through 18 July-30 July 2027), with the page noting "Applications for Summer 2027 will open soon." Fee is EUR 5,900, described as including full-board accommodation (private en-suite bedroom, 3 meals/day), in-program transport, and airport transfers within specified hours; flights, laundry and personal spending are extra. A separate, subject-specific "IE Pre-Tracks" line (Pre-Business, Pre-Law, Pre-STEM, Pre-Global Affairs, Pre-Design) exists for the same 15-17 age band. Completing the program earns "IE Pre-University Alumni" an application-fee and admissions-test-fee waiver toward a future IE Bachelor's application.
citizenship_restrictions: None stated; page notes visas apply "if applicable, for international students."
residency_restrictions: None stated on the fetched pages.
application_requirements: online application via IE's application portal
selection of one of six 2-week intake editions
selectivity_evidence: The fetched official page presents this as an enrollment/experience product with six rolling intake editions and direct 'Apply' links per edition, rather than describing an admissions jury, interview, or rejection criteria. It also states that completing the program earns 'IE Pre-University Alumni' an application-fee waiver and admissions-test fee waiver for a later IE Bachelor's application -- framing the summer program itself as a recruitment/feeder pipeline rather than an academically selective gate. No acceptance-rate or merit-review process is disclosed on the fetched pages.
